SPARQLUpdateTest#testInsertWhereInvalidT.spec: SPARQL 1.1 Update §3.1.3 (DELETE/INSERT: without USING/WITH the WHERE clause is matched "against the Graph Store"; template triples outside GRAPH go to "the default graph of the Graph Store if no WITH clause is present"), §3.1.1/§3.1.2 ("If no graph is described in the QuadData, then the default graph is presumed"), §2 (Graph Store; its unnamed graph may be "a representation of a union of other graphs"); SPARQL 1.1 Query §13.2
SPARQLUpdateTest#testInsertWhereInvalidT.note: RDF4J matches the WHERE clause over the union of all graphs and removes default-graph template/DATA triples from every graph. The engine uses the data's default graph (here: only ex:graph1/ex:graph2 metadata), as SPARQL 1.1 Update allows; the triples the test reads are in ex:graph1/ex:graph2

SPARQLUpdateTest#testDeleteFromDefaultGr.spec: SPARQL 1.1 Update §3.1.3 (GRAPH IRI and WITH IRI name a graph of the Graph Store) and §2 (Graph Store: one unnamed graph and zero or more named graphs identified by IRIs); RDF 1.1 Concepts §4
SPARQLUpdateTest#testDeleteFromDefaultGr.note: RDF4J reserves the IRIs sesame:nil and rdf4j:nil as names of the default graph, so GRAPH sesame:nil / WITH sesame:nil address the default graph. In SPARQL they are ordinary graph IRIs (an empty named graph here), so the default-graph triple stays

SPARQLUpdateTest#testUpdateSequenceWithR.spec: SPARQL 1.1 Query §19.8 [139] IRIREF ::= '<' ([^<>"{}|^`\]-[#x00-#x20])* '>' and [114] RelationalExpression ('<' NumericExpression); §19.2 longest-match tokenization
SPARQLUpdateTest#testUpdateSequenceWithR.note: The update fails with update.syntax "expected rparen" at filter(str(?company)<str(?other)): the lexer reads "<" followed by a letter as the start of an IRIREF although no ">" follows before a space. Minimal: SELECT * WHERE { BIND("a" AS ?a) FILTER(str(?a)<str(?a)) } and ASK { FILTER(1<str("a")) } give query.syntax; with spaces around < they parse; 1<2 parses. Same lookahead guard (ltCase) as https://github.com/danbri/factoidal/issues/573 (which is the converse: a valid IRIREF lexed as <); its suggested fix (scan for > before a forbidden character) would fix both
